questions.learningObjective: compute a diluted concentration using M1V1 = M2V2
questions.stem: Sample 0201: A 0.72 M stock solution is diluted by taking 30 mL and making the volume up to 144 mL. What is the final molarity?

options.misconception: inverts the dilution ratio and exaggerates the concentration
multiplies all quantities instead of conserving moles
uses the aliquot in liters but forgets the final volume

questions.explanation: Dilution conserves the number of moles, so M1 times V1 equals M2 times V2. Solving for M2 divides the product of the initial molarity and aliquot volume by the final volume. Inverting the ratio or dropping the final volume violates that conservation.
questions.hint: Moles before dilution equal moles after dilution.
